Rollback complete (09:23:30). Error rate unchanged. Odd.
Joining. 'PKIX path building failed' is a trust-chain problem, not an HttpClient problem. Checking the chain from a pod.

From a payment-adapter pod: Verify return code: 20 (unable to get local issuer certificate), issuer 'PayGate Issuing CA G3'. From the bastion with a current bundle + R2: return code 0. Leaf is valid (not before Oct 7, not after Jan 5), so this is NOT expiry. Our truststore is a baked JKS with only R1/G2.
Errors started 09:04 and only on 203.0.113.41, then .42 at ~09:11, .43 at ~09:17, .44 at ~09:24. It's a rolling change on PayGate's edges, not something we deployed.
I never received any notice from PayGate about a certificate change.
I vaguely remember an email from PayGate about TLS changes a while back?
Enabled checkout.cod_only flag to keep orders flowing (cash-on-delivery) while we fix.

Found it. Two notices (Aug 24 and Sep 24) sent to payments-vendor-alerts@, the shared mailbox Sunil owned. He left in June, nobody monitors it. They said pinned/custom truststores must add Root R2 before Oct 8.
Maintenance was announced and no customer action is expected for standard clients. Are you pinning a truststore?
We need R2 in the truststore. But I don't want to trust a root downloaded from a random URL, need the fingerprint verified out of band first.
